svg.title: Kaveon unified data intelligence architecture
svg.desc: Kaveon as it is on dev on September 12, 2026: Studio as the only front door, the API as the trusted control plane, the deterministic DLM answering from precomputed context or live SQL, and KaveonDB executing analytics over lake files while a typed record store migrates the product's own records off PostgreSQL. Solid components are implemented; dashed components are targets with their gate named.
svg.text: Unified data intelligence architecture
Talk to your data. Studio is the front door, the API is the trusted control plane, the DLM answers deterministically, KaveonDB executes over the lake.

g.text: Implemented on dev, verified on AKS
Target, with its gate named. Nothing dashed is claimed.

svg.text: Data and identity
Lake files on object storage
read by KaveonDB
Parquet · Delta (log replay, pinned version) · Iceberg
ADLS Gen2 via workload identity, or local disk
S3-compatible storage · gate: object_store reads
External SQL sources
queried by the API
Fabric SQL · Azure SQL · PostgreSQL · MySQL · StarRocks
Registered in Settings; the API runs SQL on them
KaveonDB does not federate across them.
Public datasets, curated
NYC TLC taxi · OWID energy and CO₂ · WHO COVID ·
AI benchmark tables · 504M-row synthetic telemetry
People and identity
Sign-in with Microsoft Entra ID, GitHub or Google
Roles: Viewer < Analyst < Editor < Admin
Admin by listed e-mail · visibility private, internal, published
Kaveon Studio
Next.js · the only surface a person or a browser touches
Chat
Asks the DLM; shows a clarification, an answer
from context, or a live query with its SQL
Catalog, with SQL Lab as query mode
Catalog → schema → table hub (rows, columns,
used by, DLM readiness) → query in place
Charts, dashboards, Library
ECharts · per-user pins · published dashboards
KaveonDB console
Cluster, queries, stages, memory — same roles
Settings
Connections · storage catalogs · maintenance
Trusted proxy /api/kaveon
Auth.js session → X-User-* headers signed
with KAVEON_PROXY_SECRET. The browser never
holds an API or Engine credential.
API control plane
FastAPI · verifies the proxy, resolves identity and role, routes
Deterministic DLM — no hosted model
route → resolve metric, dimension, values →
clarify on a tie → answer from context → else SQL
Client carries the frame for follow-ups; typo tolerant
80-question corpus on AKS: 80/80
Precomputed context
Per dataset: totals, every breakdown, low-cardinality
pairs, value index; HLL sketches on PostgreSQL
Rebuilt on measured data change, never on a timer
Query planes
Native catalog → Engine bridge (token, principal, role)
External source → bounded connection pool
Records and history
Datasets, charts, dashboards, saved queries,
favourites, history — outbox to KaveonDB records
Guards
Read-only SQL · platform-table denial · rate limits ·
5,000-row and statement bounds · encrypted secrets
KaveonDB
Rust · Arrow · one coordinator, N workers · TLS · Entra-validated identity · resource groups
Coordinator
Own SQL parser → plan → stage DAG → schedule
Filter and projection pushdown; join pruning
Exact statistics from Parquet footers and pinned
Delta snapshots; fail-closed broadcast decisions
Admission, memory limits, retry to another worker,
cancellation, exchange reconciliation on restart
COUNT(*) over 504M rows: 0.3 s from footers
Workers
Row-group and Delta-file splits; vectorized operators
Partial/final aggregates, exact DISTINCT, Sort/TopN,
repartitioned and broadcast hash joins, windows
Arrow IPC exchange, authenticated, byte-bounded
Spill for Sort/TopN and hash aggregates
GROUP BY over 504M rows: ~20 s on three 3-CPU workers
Storage readers
Parquet with statistics pruning · Delta log replay ·
Iceberg · ADLS Gen2 through workload identity
Byte-bounded decoded-batch cache; pinned identities
Delta checkpoints, table writes · gate: differential suite
Product record store
Typed records: datasets, charts, dashboards, DLM
definitions. Immutable, digest-verified documents;
revision-checked writes; CAS head publication on ADLS
General DML, MVCC, point-in-time restore · gate: retirement
Targets with named gates
Aggregate and join spill under pressure · exchange flow control · cost-based join order · a client wire
protocol (JDBC/ODBC) · 1.90× Trino on the declared corpus (today 1.26×) · soak, backup/restore, upgrade
Authority today: PostgreSQL kaveonmeta
Source of truth for product records while the migration runs: outbox → checkpointed backfill → exact
reconciliation → fencing → cutover. Datasets 9/9, charts 70/70, dashboards 8/8 reconciled; no cutover authorised.
The two paths, end to end
Analytical path

question in Chat → proxy stamps identity → DLM routes the dataset and resolves metric, dimension, values → on a tie, clarify → precomputed? answer in ~0.1 s → else compile SQL → Engine bridge → coordinator → workers → exact result, SQL shown
Same question, same answer, every time; no model in the loop. Live over 504M rows: 20–35 s today; the DLM builds context so the second ask is instant.
Transactional path

save a chart or dataset → API validates and writes PostgreSQL atomically with an outbox event → replay builds the typed record → revision check → digest → conditional head publication on ADLS → audit; conflicts and indeterminate outcomes surface as proofs
Product records only, not general row DML. PostgreSQL stays authoritative until reconciliation, fencing, restart and rollback evidence exist for every family.
Where it runs
Public demo — kaveon.vercel.app
Studio on Vercel · API on Azure Container Apps · Azure PostgreSQL
Flexible Server (B1ms) holds both metadata and data
No KaveonDB here yet: PostgreSQL answers every query, which is why a
504M-row table cannot live on it. Datasets are small public tables.
CI deploys every push to dev.
Qualification cluster — AKS (work tenant)
Coordinator + 3 workers · API · Studio · in-cluster PostgreSQL
Lake on ADLS Gen2, workload identity; images by digest from ACR
Where every number on this diagram was measured. Recreated from
Bicep and Helm; PostgreSQL restored from a retained disk snapshot.
Deleted at weekends for cost; rebuilt Monday.
Product host — Oracle Cloud Always Free (target)
Ampere A1, 4 OCPU / 24 GB · Compose: coordinator + workers + API
+ PostgreSQL · Caddy TLS · lake on host disk, then S3-compatible
Gate: an Oracle account and S3 reads in the Engine. Vercel keeps Studio;
API_URL moves to the host; Azure PostgreSQL retires after a verified restore.

Assessed against dev at 757606c and Engine digest 4a165e94… on kaveon-test-aks, September 12, 2026. Measurements are recorded in HANDSHAKE.md with query IDs. Where this diagram and the code disagree, the code is right and the diagram is out of date.
